newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Esat Telecom raises $35 mln to fund growth.
newsitem.headline: Esat Telecom raises $35 mln to fund growth.

text.p: Esat Telecom said on Tuesday that it had completed a $35 million funding in the U.S. this week.

The funding, by way of a high yield bond offering fixed for 9-1/2 years, with a headline rate of 12.5 percent and an effective yield of 11.9 percent, brings to $165 million the funds raised by the company over the past 14 months.

The private Irish telecommunications group said in a statement the funds would be used to build and operate local, national and international fibre optic infrastructure for its subsidiary Esat Telecom Group Plc.
The company also announced the construction of a fibre optic submarine cable between Ireland and the UK, which will have a higher capacity than any cable coming into Ireland at present.

"Since over 50 percent of all international calls from Ireland are to the UK, the construction of this link will present a very viable competitive facility for Esat Telecom and will allow the company to offer a range of broadband data services to its customers," Esat said.

Esat has signed a contract with Pirelli Cables and Systems worth 7.5 million punts for the supply and installation of the submarine optical link. The new cable will be in service by the end of February.
In conjunction with the fund raising, Esat published its results which showed a trading loss of 1.6 million Irish pounds in the first quarter of 1997 and a loss of $4.3 million for 1996.

"Start-up costs associated with establishing the infrastructure required for the creation of a telephone network and for the expansion of its customer base have contributed to the negative cash flows and operating losses of the company," Esat said.

The total net loss for the first three months of 1997 was eight million Irish pounds, reflecting investment in infrastructure, debt servicing and the on-going capital investment in Esat Digifone which operates Ireland's second mobile 'phone network.
Esat said that it had purchased an additional five percent holding in Esat Digifone as has Norway's Telenor.
The two companies now hold 45 percent each of Esat Digifone with the remaining 10 percent held by IIU Nominees Ltd.

Esat said it had paid 2.9 million Irish pounds to IIU for the five percent stake as well as an additional payment reflecting the advances made by IIU to the capital investment in Esat Digifone relating to the five percent.
Esat said Esat Digifone has been "extremely successful" since its establishment five months ago and has gained 45,000 customers, representing 23 percent of the GSM market.
